name: Grammarly
tagline: Grammar, clarity, tone, and AI writing assistant across apps

pricing.notes: Official plan URL checked; public 2026 coverage commonly references Grammarly Pro/Premium around $30/month, with annual pricing lower and branding evolving under Superhuman.

verdictSummary: You can build grammar checks and rewrites, but Grammarly's moat is cross-app extensions, inline UX, enterprise controls, writing telemetry, and long-running language quality.
coreLoopDIY: Run text through LanguageTool plus an LLM rewrite/tone checker, expose a browser extension or local editor.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because suggestions appear inside the apps where writing actually happens.

priorArt.name: LanguageTool
priorArt.desc: Open-source grammar and style checker and the primary Grammarly-like prior art.

notes: An important 'kinda': grammar checking is open-source, cross-app UX is the hard product.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Grammarly (Grammar, clarity, tone, and AI writing assistant across apps). Requirements:

- Core loop: Run text through LanguageTool plus an LLM rewrite/tone checker, expose a browser extension or local editor.
- Needs: grammar engine/API.
- Needs: LLM API.
- Needs: browser extension.
- Needs: optional desktop accessibility layer.
- Needs: user dictionary.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: inline suggestions everywhere; document/email integrations; tone/brand controls.
